dependencyDashboardHeader:
This issue lists the dependency updates the bot (Renovate) found for this repository, and what each one is waiting for. Open the guide below before ticking a box. > [!IMPORTANT] > - **A ticked box acts at the bot's next run** (runs start at 01:00 and 13:00 Amman time), not right away. > - **Ticking skips this repository's weekly window and the limit of 5 open bot PRs.** Every PR the bot opens still goes through verify. > - **The bold box at the end of a section acts on every item in that section at once.**
Guide: what each section lists, and what ticking a box does | Section | What it lists | What ticking a box does | |---|---|---| | **Pending Approval** | Updates a person has to decide on. These are major versions (any update that changes the first version number), 0.x minor versions, and on mobile repos the Android build toolchain (Gradle, Android Gradle Plugin, Kotlin) and the Flutter SDK. They never merge by themselves. | Opens that PR at the next run. Verify tests it, then a person reviews and merges it. "Create all pending approval PRs at once" opens every update listed here. | | **Awaiting Schedule** | Routine updates found outside this repository's weekly window (one weekday, 00:00 to 09:00 Amman time). They wait for the window. | Opens the PR at the next run instead of in the window. "Create all awaiting schedule PRs at once" does that for every update listed here. | | **Pending Status Checks** | Updates whose new version is too recent: published less than 7 days ago (npm) or 3 days ago (other sources). The wait is the defence against a freshly compromised release. Security fixes already skip it. | ⚠️ Opens the PR now with that new version. **This skips the safety wait and the approval step.** **Don't use it**: if an update is urgent, ask DevOps. The daily digest names everyone who ticks it. | | **Rate-Limited** | Updates held back because 5 bot PRs are already open. | Opens the PR anyway. "Create all rate-limited PRs at once" opens every update listed here. | | **Open** | Updates that already have a PR. | Rebuilds that PR on top of the latest base branch. "Rebase all open PRs at once" does that for every PR listed here. | | **PR Edited (Blocked)** | PRs that someone pushed their own commits to. The bot stops updating them. | Throws those commits away and rebuilds the PR from scratch. | | **PR Closed (Blocked)** | Updates whose PR was closed without merging. The bot does not propose that version again. | Opens the PR again. | | **Errored** | Updates where the bot hit an error. They are retried at every run. | Retries at the next run. | | **Other Branches** | Updates in progress that have no PR yet. | Opens the PR. | | **Repository Problems** | Warnings about the bot's setup for this repository. | No box. Nothing to do on your side. Tell the maintainers if a warning stays. | | **Deprecations / Replacements**, **Abandoned Dependencies** | Dependencies that are deprecated, replaced by another package, or no longer released. | No box. Plan to move off them. | | **Detected Dependencies** | Every dependency the bot found, per file. | No box. | **After a PR opens.** Verify builds and tests it. Routine (non-major) updates and the weekly lock file refresh merge by themselves once verify is green. Everything listed under Pending Approval, and the iOS toolchain, always waits for a person.
More on the dashboard: [Renovate's Dependency Dashboard docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/dashboard/).

customManagers.description: Yarn 1 pinned in Dockerfiles: node:26 images no longer include Yarn, so Dockerfiles install it (RUN command -v yarn >/dev/null || npm install -g yarn@<version>). Renovate keeps that pin current, within Yarn 1 (the org standard; see the yarn rule below)

packageRules.description: Weekly routine group: non-breaking updates move together so lockstep sets cannot split; 0.x patches are non-breaking in practice and automerge. An update whose leading version number changes is kept out (see the cross-major rule below)
npm soak against compromised fresh releases

Docker registries give Renovate no release timestamps, and Renovate 44 treats an update without one as too young forever (minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour timestamp-required), so it never updated a base image (FROM node, dotnet, nginx) and dropped them from branches silently. The age of a Docker tag cannot be measured: let those updates through

A lock file refresh has no release timestamp either, so under timestamp-required its renovate/stability-days stayed pending forever. Where Renovate merges by itself (platformAutomerge off: repos whose develop needs the App's approval bypass) it waits for every status, so no lock refresh ever merged there. The age gate in front of the registries already holds every lock version to 7 days
0.x minors can break: own branch, dashboard approval, never automerged (regex matcher works for every datasource, unlike isBreaking)
Yarn 1 is the org standard (yarn.lock v1): the Dockerfile pin never leaves 1.x
Major updates need a human: dashboard approval, never automerged

Cross-major guard: Renovate can type a major as minor or patch. A NuGet bare version is a minimum, and when the current release is deprecated Renovate measures from the oldest non-deprecated one (MSTest 3.6.4 -> 4.5.2 was typed 4.5.1 -> 4.5.2, patch). So the leading number of the version actually written decides: if it changes, treat the update as a major
